rationale: The text describes reports, data export, and analytics features, supporting a conventional analytics classification. However, 'Data Driven Attribution' does not specify how attribution is produced, so the possibility of AI-dependent functionality cannot be resolved from the description alone; the non-AI decision is weak and forced.
evidence_spans: With Google Analytics 360, your team can access advanced tools, like Unsampled Reports, BigQuery Export, and Data Driven Attribution, in addition to all the standard Analytics features and reports.
conflict_response: Both proposals classify the offering as non-AI, but the blind proposal treats the evidence as supported. The parent specifically flags Data Driven Attribution: the phrase names a capability but gives no implementation details. Under the text-only boundary, it does not establish AI, and it also leaves unresolved whether attribution is AI-dependent. I therefore retain non-AI as the best-supported binary choice while marking it weak and forced, rather than treating agreement or product knowledge as evidence.
